identity.name: Speedmaster Moonwatch Professional
identity.one_liner: The current-production hand-wound Moonwatch, updated in January 2021 with the Co-Axial Master Chronometer caliber 3861 while keeping the hesalite crystal and case profile of the earlier caliber 1861 reference.

provenance_events.description: The Speedmaster Moonwatch Professional with calibre 3861 — co-axial escapement, Master Chronometer, 50m water resistance — becomes the modern Moonwatch baseline, replacing the 1861 line that ran 1996-2021.

narrative.story: Omega introduced this reference in January 2021 as the first Speedmaster Professional to carry a Co-Axial escapement, replacing the outgoing caliber 1861 with the Master Chronometer-certified caliber 3861 while keeping the hesalite crystal, dot-over-90 bezel, and asymmetrical case shape associated with the watch NASA qualified for spaceflight in 1965. The movement adds a silicon balance spring and resistance to magnetic fields up to 15,000 gauss but stays hand-wound, so the winding feel and 12-hour chronograph layout match the pre-2021 Moonwatch rather than switching to an automatic caliber. It is the reference Omega ships as the standard steel Moonwatch today, alongside sapphire-crystal and other case-material variants built on the same caliber 3861 movement.
narrative.collector_notes: Omega sells several parallel caliber 3861 references on this case — hesalite or sapphire crystal, bracelet or strap — so confirm the exact reference number rather than assuming 'Moonwatch' means this specific hesalite-on-bracelet execution. Because the watch remains in production, the originality checks that matter on vintage Speedmasters (relumed hands, replaced pushers, mismatched serials) don't apply yet.
